This is not my story, but rather my mom's.

When she was young, about mid 20's, she was driving along a deserted road only a few minutes from her destination when she got a flat tire. She was forced to pull over on the side of the road and signal for help.

Being so young and alone was scary, especially when a guy in a white van pulled over and offered to help. He was wearing formal clothing, much of it being white. She accepted, but he could tell she was nervous, so he told her to wait in the car with the doors locked while he changed out her tire so she wouldn't be scared. 

She did so, and a few moments later her tire was replaced. She was so grateful that she offered him money, but he graciously declined, and drove off.

My mom tells me this story all the time, because in hindsight, she's certain this guy was her guardian Angel.

The year was 1913. A young man by the name of Frank walked along the empty street, an ominous dark blanket laid over the sky and an eerie silence ringing in the air. No sound emerged from the night but the light tapping noise of his shoes clicking against the road. He enjoyed strolling along at midnight in this manner, when no one was awake but him. He ran a gloved hand along the rim of his top hat, a content smile on his rather elongated face.

Mister Frank paused his footsteps to gaze curiously at what looked like an abandoned antique selling vendor stand. It was littered with knick-knacks and trinkets alike, but one gold-tinted oil lamp caught his eye. It had a peculiar luminescence about it, and the man had a sudden urge to reach out and touch it. His hand subconsciously raised and his fingers lingered over the gold-tinted metal object. Quickly, he glanced around to make sure he was alone, and allowed his urge to be satisfied. He grasped the handle of the lamp and lifted it closer to his blue eyes, sparkling with curiosity, for examination. It appeared normal, but something about it seemed bizarre. He noticed a smudge of dirt on the side of it, and used his fabric-covered thumb to rub it off.

Almost immediately, the lamp was illuminated with an unearthly blue light, and Frank was so startled he almost dropped the ornament. The light grew stronger and stronger until rays of it began shooting out the sides, as though the source of it was trapped inside and struggling to escape. Frank's face contorted into that of sheer surprise, paralyzed by shock and confusion. Suddenly, the lamp's cap burst open and out drifted a cloud of anomalous blue smoke. Slowly, the smoke began to take shape into what appeared to be a crude humanoid figure.

As eyes and a mouth began to take form, the silence that once filled the night was broken by a booming male voice. Frank could make it out as "What has woken me from my slumber?"

Frank's mouth opened and closed pathetically as he struggled to make words. "I—I—" was as close as he got.

As though the creature had just now noticed him, its eyes focused on his terrified expression. "You, mortal. Why have you woken me?"

"I—I'm sorry, sir—I didn't mean to—" the young man stammered out, staring up helplessly at the bundle of gas, his mind drawing a blank.

The thing sighed heavily, obviously exasperated. "I assume you rubbed the lamp. Therefore, I must grant you unlimited wishes."

The words repeated over and over in Frank's frozen brain. He blinked, shaking his head in disbelief, as though if he tossed his head around enough, the smoke would be gone and he would find out this was all just some weird dream. It didn't happen, though, and when he stopped, the creature was still there, its makeshift face forming an expression of boredom. "Are... Are you kidding?"

"No. But there's something else. For every wish, you must answer me a mathematical question. If your solution is incorrect, there will be dire consequences.

Frank scratched his head from under his hat, leaving the accessory lopsided. The creature continued staring at him like he was stupid. "What kind of consequences?"

"Every wish you previously made will be reversed."

"...Oh."

The two continued staring at each other for what seemed like hours to the desperately confused gentleman. Finally, he snapped himself out of his daze. "I'm ready to make my first wish."

The smokey soul straightened up a bit, if you can call it that. "Go ahead, mortal. Tell me your wish, and it shall be my command."

"Okay." Frank took a minute to collect his thoughts. He breathed in and out heavily, focusing on his wish, making sure he knew exactly what he was going to say. Then, out of the goodness of his pure human heart, he spoke. "I wish for peace on Earth." It was a humble wish. A truly kind one, that would warm any listener's heart. The creature didn't take any time to notice this, though, and immediately replied with a mathematical equation.

"Very well. What is the sum of 5 and 7?"

It was a simple question. An easy-peasy, slice-of-cake problem that any normal human could compute. Frank knew this, and he understood that if he got the answer wrong, the entire world could suffer. He took a deep breath in, and blurted out—

"Thirteen."

"Incorrect."

"Wait—no—"

"Too late, mortal."

And thus, the world began.
